newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Thousands of Timorese prepare to march in Dili.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Timorese prepare to march in Dili.

text.p: Thousands of Timorese prepared to march from outside the University of East Timor on Thursday as protests in support of Nobel laureate Bishop Carlos Belo in the East Timorese capital Dili entered their third day.

"The situation is still going ahead like yesterday. Those who are here are not only university students but all people of Catholic faith. There are thousands of people," a member of the university staff told Reuters.

"They are carrying banners and want to go to the regional parliament and then to the governor's office like yesterday but in a safe and orderly way, they do not want to throw stones or hit people," said the staff member, who did not identify himself.

He said one of the banners he could see read "Viva Bishop Belo" and added the situation was still calm with no confrontation with security forces. The crowd was lined up and ready to leave at around 9.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), he said.

On Wednesday, students who had gathered at the university campus marched to the parliament where they threw stones, breaking some of the building's windows. Some reports said one legislator's car was also damaged.
The protests have been sparked by criticism in an Indonesian newspaper against reported comments made by Belo to a German magazine that Indonesians had treated East Timorese like "dogs".
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and unilaterally declared the territory its 27th province the following year.
The protests started after students met with members of the official National Commission of Human Rights on Monday at the university.
The commission called for calm on Wednesday and said Belo should be given an opportunity to explain his position.
"The commission is of the opinion that excessive action and denunciation without any legal basis is a violation of human rights," it said in a media statement.
